Verify password_hash matches the provided password using bcrypt/Argon2 verification. Check that deleted_at is null (account not soft deleted). If validation succeeds, issue new JWT access and refresh tokens with member.id and email in payload. Create new session record in todo_app_member_sessions table with ip, href, referrer from request headers. operations.description:
Authenticates a member by validating email and password credentials against the todo_app_members table.

The login process accepts an email address and password. The system performs case-insensitive lookup of the email in todo_app_members.email to locate the corresponding member account. If the account exists and is active (deleted_at is null), the system verifies the provided password against the stored password_hash using secure password verification (bcrypt or Argon2).

Upon successful authentication, the system issues JWT tokens containing the member's ID and email in the payload. A new session record is created in the todo_app_member_sessions table, capturing the request's IP address, href (login page URL), and referrer header for security auditing. The access token is short-lived (15 minutes) while the refresh token has a longer lifetime (7 days) to enable seamless token renewal without re-authentication.

For security, the system enforces a single active session policy - if a member is already logged in on another device, the existing session is terminated and replaced with the new one. This prevents credential sharing and ensures session freshness. Passwords are never returned in the response, only JWT tokens and minimal member information.

responseBody.description: Authentication tokens and member information after successful login

operations.specification: Renew expired JWT access token using refresh token. Validate refresh token signature and expiration using the same signing key used for token issuance. Extract member.id from refresh token payload. Look up member in todo_app_members to verify account still exists and is active (deleted_at is null). If validation succeeds, issue new access token (15 min) and optionally refresh token. Create new session record in todo_app_member_sessions. Return authorized response with refreshed tokens. If refresh token is expired, tampered with, or member account is deleted, reject with 401 unauthorized.
operations.description:
Refreshes an expired JWT access token to maintain authenticated session without requiring re-login.

The refresh operation validates the refresh token that was issued during the original login or previous refresh. The system verifies the token's signature using the secure signing algorithm and checks the expiration time. If valid, the system extracts the member ID from the token payload and verifies the member account still exists and is active in the todo_app_members table.

Upon successful validation, the system issues a new access token (valid for 15 minutes) that allows continued access to protected API endpoints. A new session record is created in todo_app_member_sessions to maintain the audit trail. The refresh token may also be renewed depending on security policy.

Security considerations: The refresh token endpoint implements rate limiting to prevent abuse. If a refresh token is expired, tampered with, or the member account has been deleted, the request is rejected with a 401 Unauthorized response. This ensures that compromised or expired tokens cannot be used to maintain unauthorized access.

responseBody.description: New authentication tokens after successful refresh

operations.description:
Update the authenticated member's profile display name in the `todo_app_user_profiles` table.

This operation allows a logged-in user to change their display name, which is visible across all user-facing features of the application. The display name is a customizable identifier stored in the `todo_app_user_profiles` table that the user can modify at any time.

The operation validates the new display name against business rules: it must be non-empty, cannot contain prohibited characters, and must not exceed the maximum allowed length. The system enforces a daily change limit (maximum one change per 24 hours) tracked in the `todo_app_user_profiles.last_display_name_change_at` field to prevent abuse.

Only the account owner can update their own profile. The operation requires member authentication and will reject any unauthenticated requests. Cross-user profile access is strictly prohibited and will be denied.

Upon successful validation and update, the new display name is persisted to the `todo_app_user_profiles` table immediately and reflected across all todos, edit history entries, and other user-related displays where the display name appears.
operations.specification:
1. Authenticate the requesting user via session token (member actor required)
2. Extract displayName from request body
3. Validate displayName is non-empty string (reject empty or whitespace-only)
4. Validate displayName does not exceed 50 characters (ITodoAppUserProfile.displayName maxLength)
5. Validate displayName does not contain prohibited characters (alphanumeric, spaces, underscores, hyphens only)
6. Check daily change limit from ITodoAppUserProfile.lastDisplayNameChange timestamp
7. If all validations pass, update todo_app_user_profiles.displayName with new value
8. Update todo_app_user_profiles.lastDisplayNameChange to current datetime
9. Return updated profile object with new displayName
10. If validation fails, return 400 error with specific validation message

requestBody.description: Profile update data containing the new display name

responseBody.description: Updated user profile with the new display name

operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of authentication sessions for the authenticated member across all devices.

This operation provides visibility into the member's active and expired authentication sessions, enabling them to monitor device access and manage security. Sessions are retrieved from the todo_app_member_sessions table with support for filtering by status, date ranges, and IP address.

Search capabilities include filtering by session status (active/expired), creation date range, expiration date range, and specific IP addresses. Results are paginated using cursor-based pagination for efficient handling of large session histories.

Security validation ensures members can only access their own sessions. The authenticated member's ID from the JWT session claim is matched against session records. If the member is not found or authentication fails, a 404 Not Found error is returned.
operations.name: index

requestBody.description: Search criteria and pagination parameters for session listing

responseBody.description: Paginated list of member session summaries

operations.specification:
Query the todo_app_member_sessions table where todo_app_member_id matches the authenticated user's ID (from JWT session claim).

Apply the following filters:
- status: if 'active', filter sessions where expired_at > NOW(); if 'expired', filter where expired_at <= NOW()
- created_after: filter sessions where created_at >= value
- created_before: filter sessions where created_at <= value
- expired_after: filter sessions where expired_at >= value
- expired_before: filter sessions where expired_at <= value
- ip: exact match on IP address field

Apply ordering:
- sortBy: 'created_at' or 'expired_at'
- sortOrder: 'asc' or 'desc'
- nullsLast: when sorting by date fields, sessions without values appear last

Apply cursor-based pagination:
- cursor: optional pagination token from previous page
- direction: 'forward' (after cursor) or 'backward' (before cursor)
- take: number of records to return (default: 20, max: 100)

Return fields: id, todo_app_member_id, ip, href, referrer, created_at, expired_at, status (computed: active|expired)

Security: Authorize only if the authenticated member's ID matches the query criteria. Throw 404 Not Found if member not found.

operations.description:
Retrieve detailed information about a specific member session.

This operation returns comprehensive session metadata including the authenticated member's identification, connection details from the login request, and temporal fields for session lifecycle tracking.

The session record contains valuable audit information such as the client IP address, request URL, and referrer that was captured when the member logged in. This data is useful for security monitoring, anomaly detection, and troubleshooting authentication issues.

Members can only view their own sessions. The system enforces strict data isolation to ensure that one member cannot access session information belonging to another member.

Session information includes the creation timestamp, expiration timestamp, and the associated member ID. Expired sessions remain in the database as historical audit records, while active sessions can be identified by comparing the current time against the expiration timestamp.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query the todo_app_member_sessions table for the session record matching the provided sessionId UUID.

1. Validate that sessionId is a valid UUID format
2. Retrieve the session record including all fields: id, todo_app_member_id, ip, href, referrer, created_at, expired_at
3. Include the related member reference (todo_app_member_id)
4. Enforce authorization: verify the current authenticated member's ID matches the todo_app_member_id on the session record
5. Return 404 if the session does not exist
6. Return 403 if the authenticated member is not the owner of the session
7. Serialize the session object with proper DateTime formatting for created_at and expired_at
8. Include all session fields in the response: id, todoAppMemberId, ip, href, referrer, createdAt, expiredAt

responseBody.description: Detailed session information including authentication metadata and connection details

parameters.name: sessionId
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the session to retrieve

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated and filtered list of email verification records for the todo application.

This operation provides administrative visibility into email verification requests across all member accounts. It supports filtering by verification status (pending, completed, expired), date range constraints, and cursor-based pagination for efficient large dataset traversal.

Each record includes the member association, token information (hashed for security), expiration details, and verification outcome. The response is optimized for admin dashboard display with summary fields only.

Security Note: This operation is restricted to administrative actors. All token values are returned in hashed form only to prevent exposure of verification secrets.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query todo_app_member_email_verifications table with pagination and filtering.

Apply search filters:
- status: filter by verification state (pending, completed, expired)
- createdAfter: filter records created after specified datetime
- createdBefore: filter records created before specified datetime
- memberId: filter by specific member's verifications
- memberEmail: partial match on associated member's email

Apply pagination:
- cursor: optional cursor for cursor-based pagination
- pageSize: number of records per page (default: 50, max: 100)
- direction: pagination direction (forward or backward)

Sort results by:
- sortBy: field name (createdAt, expiresAt, status)
- sortOrder: ascending or descending

Join with todo_app_members for email field when memberId filter not provided.

Return hashed token only - never expose raw verification tokens.

Apply administrative authorization check before query execution.

requestBody.description: Search criteria, pagination parameters, and sort options for email verifications list

responseBody.description: Paginated list of email verification summaries

operations.description:
Retrieve a specific email verification token by its unique identifier.

This operation returns the complete details of an email verification token, including the token value, expiration timestamp, usage status, and associated member account reference. The verification token is generated during member registration and is used to validate email addresses before granting full account access.

The endpoint requires authenticated member access. Members can only retrieve verification tokens associated with their own account. This restriction is enforced at the service layer to prevent unauthorized access to other users' verification data.

The token value is included in the response but should be treated as sensitive information. Applications should handle this data according to their security policies.

Related operations:
- POST /auth/register - Creates a new verification token during account registration
- POST /auth/verify-email - Uses a verification token to complete email verification
- GET /auth/profile - Access current member's account information
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query the todo_app_member_email_verifications table for the record matching the verificationId path parameter.

Authorization:
1. Extract authenticated member ID from the session token
2. Verify that the verification token's todo_app_member_id matches the authenticated member's ID
3. Return 403 Forbidden if member does not own this verification token

Query Logic:
- Use UUID-based lookup on the id field
- Include all fields: id, todo_app_member_id, token, expires_at, used, used_at, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at
- Verify record is not soft-deleted (deleted_at is null)

Error Handling:
- Return 404 Not Found if verification token does not exist
- Return 403 Forbidden if authenticated member does not own this token
- Return 401 Unauthorized if no valid session token provided

Security Considerations:
- Token value should be redacted from responses in production environments
- Rate limiting should be applied to prevent enumeration attacks
- Audit log entry should be created for this retrieval operation

responseBody.description: Email verification token details

parameters.name: verificationId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the email verification token to retrieve

operations.description:
Request a password reset token for member account recovery.

This endpoint initiates the password recovery process by accepting a member's email address and creating a secure, temporary password reset token. The token is stored in the todo_app_member_password_resets table and sent to the member's registered email address as a reset link.

The operation validates that the email format is correct before processing the request. For security reasons, the response is identical whether the email address exists in the system or not, preventing enumeration attacks that could reveal valid member accounts.

Related operations:
- POST /todoApp/member/login - Standard member authentication
- PUT /todoApp/member/password - Password change after successful token verification
- GET /todoApp/member/register - Member account registration
operations.name: requestReset
operations.specification: Accept email address in request body. Validate email format using RFC 5322 standard. If email is valid format, search for matching member account in todo_app_members table by email field (case-insensitive). Whether member exists or not, generate a cryptographically secure random token (minimum 32 bytes, encoded as hexadecimal or URL-safe base64). Calculate expiration time by adding the configured token lifetime (default: 1 hour) to current UTC timestamp. Create new todo_app_member_password_resets record with: id (auto-generated UUID), todo_app_member_id (found member ID or null if email not found), token (generated), expires_at (calculated), created_at (current timestamp), updated_at (current timestamp). Send password reset email containing the secure reset link with token as query parameter. Return success response indicating reset email was sent. Do not reveal whether the email was found in the database. Ensure all database operations occur within a single transaction. Log the password reset request in the audit trail with timestamp, email address (hashed if PII concerns), and operation result. Implement rate limiting on this endpoint to prevent abuse (e.g., maximum 5 requests per hour per IP address, maximum 20 requests per day per IP address).

responseBody.description: Confirmation that password reset request was processed. Contains the reset ID for tracking and indicates whether the request was accepted. Note: Response does not reveal whether the email address exists in the system.

requestBody.description: Email address for the member account requesting password reset. The email must be in valid format and will be used to locate the member account.

operations.description:
Retrieve the status and metadata of a password reset token.

This endpoint provides diagnostic information about a password reset token request, including whether the token is active, expired, or has been used. It returns verification status without exposing the actual token value for security purposes.

The operation is typically used by internal systems to verify token validity during password recovery flows, or by administrators for audit purposes. Each password reset token is associated with a specific member account and can only be accessed by that member.

Password reset tokens are generated when a member requests a password reset via email. The token is valid for a limited duration (typically 1-24 hours) and is invalidated after successful password reset or expiration.

Note: This endpoint returns verification status and metadata only. The actual reset token value is not included in the response for security reasons.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query the todo_app_member_password_resets table for the record with the specified resetId.

1. Verify the requesting member is authenticated.
2. Validate that the resetId exists in the database.
3. Verify the password reset token belongs to the authenticated member by checking todo_app_member_id matches.
4. Check if the token is expired by comparing expires_at with current time.
5. Check if the token has been soft-deleted by checking deleted_at.
6. Return token metadata including: id, creation time, expiration time, and active status.
7. Do NOT return the actual token value for security.
8. If the member does not own this password reset token, return 404 Forbidden.
9. If the token is not found, return 404 Not Found.

Business logic:
- Only the member who owns the password reset token can view its status.
- Expired or used tokens should still be retrievable but marked as inactive.
- Soft-deleted tokens (deleted_at is non-null) are considered invalid.

Return fields:
- id: The password reset token ID (UUID)
- created_at: When the token was generated
- expires_at: When the token becomes invalid
- isActive: Boolean indicating if the token is currently valid (not expired, not deleted)

This is a read-only diagnostic operation. It does not modify any data.

responseBody.description: Password reset token status and metadata

parameters.name: resetId
parameters.description: The UUID identifier of the password reset token to check.

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of todos belonging to the authenticated user.

This operation provides advanced list capabilities with filtering by completion status (all, complete, incomplete) and sorting options for creation date, start date, or due date. Todos without start or due dates will appear at the end of the list when sorting by those date fields.

The response includes paginated results with cursor-based navigation for efficient large result set handling. Each todo item contains essential information including title, completion status, dates, and ID for display in todo list views.

Only authenticated member users can access this endpoint. Guests are restricted from viewing any todos. Users can only retrieve todos belonging to their own account - cross-user access is strictly enforced.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query todo_app_todos table where userId matches the authenticated member's ID.

Security validation ensures the authenticated user owns the target todo. Access to another user's todos is strictly prohibited - the system will reject any attempt to retrieve todos not belonging to the requesting user.

operations.description:
Create a new todo item for the authenticated member account.

This operation creates a todo with the required title field and optional description, start date, and due date fields. The todo is automatically associated with the authenticated member's account and is private - only the creating member can view, edit, or delete it.

Upon creation, the todo is marked as incomplete (is_complete: false) by default and not deleted (is_deleted: false). System-managed fields including the unique identifier and timestamps (created_at, updated_at) are automatically generated by the database.

The authenticated member must have valid authentication credentials. Guest users without a member account cannot create todos and will receive an access denied error.

Create a new record in the todo_app_todos table with the following logic:

1. Extract authenticated member ID from the session context (not from request body)
2. Validate that the request body contains a non-empty, non-whitespace title string
3. Set member_id to the authenticated member's ID
4. Set title from the request body
5. Set optional fields (description, start_date, due_date) from request body if provided, otherwise leave as null
6. Set is_complete to false (default value)
7. Set is_deleted to false (default value)
8. Set created_at and updated_at to the current UTC timestamp
9. Set deleted_at to null (not deleted)
10. Insert the record into todo_app_todos table
11. Return the newly created todo with all fields including the generated id

operations.description:
Update an existing todo's details (title, description, start date, or due date).

This operation allows authenticated members to modify their own todo records. Any field modification triggers automatic creation of an EditHistory entry to maintain an audit trail of changes.

The authenticated user MUST own the target todo - cross-user updates are rejected with an access denied error. The todo must also not be soft-deleted (in trash) for this operation to succeed.

All modifications are validated against business rules: title is required and cannot be empty, start date must not be after due date if both are provided. Upon successful update, the todo's updatedAt timestamp is automatically refreshed.

Verify the authenticated member's ID matches the todo's userId field to enforce ownership.
Reject with 403 Forbidden if ownership verification fails.

Begin database transaction.
Update only the provided fields in the todo record.
IF any field changed, insert new entry into todo_app_edit_histories with previous and new values for modified fields.
IF todo's isComplete status changed due to edit history, mark that in history entry.
Commit transaction.
Return the updated todo record with all current values including refreshed updatedAt timestamp.

Error handling:
- 401 Unauthorized if no authentication token provided
- 403 Forbidden if user does not own the todo
- 404 Not Found if todo doesn't exist or is in trash

operations.description:
Soft delete a todo by moving it to trash.

This operation removes the todo from the normal todo list and moves it to the trash area. The todo's data is preserved including title, description, dates, completion status, and all associated edit history entries. Deleted todos are no longer visible in the normal todo list but can be accessed through the trash view.

Only the todo owner can delete their own todos. The operation validates that the authenticated member owns the todo before performing the deletion. If the todo does not exist or the member does not own it, the request is rejected.

The soft delete is reversible through the trash restoration feature. Deleted todos retain all their original data and edit history for potential restoration.

After deletion, the todo's is_deleted flag is set to true and the deleted_at timestamp is recorded. The todo appears in the trash list (GET /todos/trash) but not in the normal todo list.

Related operations:
- GET /todos - Lists active todos (non-deleted)
- GET /todos/trash - Lists deleted todos in trash
- PUT /todos/{id}/restore - Restores a todo from trash
- DELETE /todos/{id} (trash) - Permanently deletes a todo from trash
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
1. Validate authenticated member owns the todo identified by todoId
2. Query todo_app_todos WHERE id = todoId AND member_id = authenticated_member_id
3. If todo not found or ownership validation fails, return 404 or 403 error
4. Update todo record: set is_deleted=true, set deleted_at=current timestamp
5. Preserve all other fields and relationships (editHistories cascade)
6. Return updated todo object showing deleted state with is_deleted=true and deleted_at timestamp
7. Do NOT delete edit history entries - they are preserved for potential restoration
8. Validation: Ensure todoId is valid UUID format

operations.description:
Retrieve the current authenticated member's profile information including their email address and display name.

This operation returns the user's profile details from the todo_app_members table, providing essential account information for display in user-facing interfaces.

The response includes the user's email address (used for authentication), their display name (used for personalization and user identification), and account metadata including creation and update timestamps. The deleted_at field indicates if the account has been marked for deletion.

This endpoint requires member authentication and returns only the authenticated user's own profile data with strict privacy isolation. Cross-user profile access is not permitted. The operation uses soft deletion tracking via the deleted_at field for account lifecycle management.

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of the authenticated member's deleted todos from trash.

This operation returns todos that have been soft-deleted (is_deleted=true) and moved to the trash folder. Each deleted todo is displayed with its original creation date, deletion timestamp, title, and completion status from before deletion.

The list supports filtering by the todo's completion status before deletion and sorting by creation date, start date, or due date. Todos without date values are consistently placed at the end of sorted results.

Only the owner of each todo can view their trash list. Cross-user access is prevented by ownership validation enforced through member authentication.

If no deleted todos exist for the member, an empty list is returned with null cursors. The response includes nextCursor and previousCursor for cursor-based navigation through paginated results.

- sortOrder: ascending (earliest/oldest first) or descending (latest/newest first)

- Query with LIMIT (page size) and WHERE clause for pagination key comparison

operations.description:
Restore a todo from the trash to the normal todo list, preserving all original data and metadata.

This operation moves a soft-deleted todo back to the active todo list, restoring its completion status, dates, title, description, and complete edit history. The todo becomes fully functional again and appears in the user's normal todo list view.

The system validates that the authenticated user owns the todo being restored and that the todo exists in the trash. Ownership enforcement ensures users can only restore their own deleted todos, maintaining data isolation.

When a todo is restored, it retains its original creation date rather than being assigned a new timestamp, preserving the chronological integrity of the user's todo timeline.

1. Authenticate the requesting user and validate session
2. Retrieve todo from todo_app_todos where id = todoId AND isDeleted = true
3. Validate that the todo's userId matches the authenticated user's id
4. If todo not found or ownership mismatch, return 404 Not Found or 403 Forbidden
5. Set isDeleted = false to restore the todo to normal list
6. Return the complete todo record including all fields: id, title, description, startDate, dueDate, isComplete, createdAt, updatedAt, userId
7. Ensure edit history entries remain associated with the restored todo through the todoId foreign key
8. Make the operation idempotent - if the todo is already restored, return the current state without error

operations.description:
Retrieve the complete edit history for a specific todo, displaying an audit trail of all modifications made to that todo.

This operation provides access to the full history of changes made to a todo, including timestamps, the member who made each edit, and the previous and new values for every field that was modified (title, description, start date, due date).

History entries are automatically created by the system whenever a todo is edited and are immutable once created. Each entry records the exact values before and after the change, allowing users to track the evolution of their todo over time.

Access to edit history is restricted to the owner of the todo. Users cannot view edit history for todos owned by other users, even if they know the todo ID. The system validates ownership before returning any history data.

History entries are returned in chronological order with the most recent edits appearing first, making it easy to see the progression of changes to a todo.
operations.name: getByTodoid
operations.specification:
Query the todo_app_edit_histories table filtered by todo_app_todos_id matching the todoId path parameter.

Validate that:
1. The todo exists and belongs to the authenticated member (todo_app_member_id)
2. The authenticated user has ownership of the todo

If the todo does not exist, return 404 Not Found.
If the todo belongs to another user, return 403 Forbidden.

Query all edit history entries for the todo, ordered by created_at descending (most recent first).

Return an array of ITodoAppEditHistory objects, each containing:
- id: UUID of the history entry
- todoAppTodosId: UUID of the parent todo
- todoAppMemberId: UUID of the member who made the edit
- createdAt: DateTime timestamp of when the edit occurred
- previousTitle: string | null (value before edit if title changed)
- newTitle: string | null (value after edit if title changed)
- previousDescription: string | null (value before edit if description changed)
- newDescription: string | null (value after edit if description changed)
- previousStartDate: DateTime | null (value before edit if start date changed)
- newStartDate: DateTime | null (value after edit if start date changed)
- previousDueDate: DateTime | null (value before edit if due date changed)
- newDueDate: DateTime | null (value after edit if due date changed)

If no history entries exist for the todo (e.g., it was never edited), return an empty array.

This operation provides users with a complete audit trail of every change made to their todo, including modifications to the title, description, start date, and due date. Each history entry records when the edit occurred, which field was changed, and the previous and new values.

Users can only access edit history for todos they own. The system enforces strict privacy isolation, rejecting any requests for todos belonging to other users. History entries are immutable once created and cannot be modified or deleted individually.

The response includes comprehensive filtering options for date ranges, field types, and value patterns, along with configurable pagination and sorting controls for efficient navigation through large edit histories.

This operation returns detailed information about a single edit that was made to a todo, including the timestamp of the change, the member who made it, and the before/after values for any fields that were modified (title, description, start date, due date).

Edit history entries are automatically created by the system whenever a todo is edited. They serve as an immutable audit log showing exactly what changed, when it changed, and who made the change. Users can view the complete history of their todos to understand how tasks have evolved over time.

2. Verify the associated todo exists
3. Verify the authenticated member owns the todo (todo_app_todos.todo_app_member_id = member.id)

- previous_title, new_title
- previous_description, new_description
- previous_start_date, new_start_date
- previous_due_date, new_due_date

# Multi-User Todo Application - E2E Test Requirements

## Authentication Tests
- Test user registration with valid email and password
- Test user login with valid credentials
- Test user logout functionality
- Test password change operation
- Test account deletion (including verification that all todos are removed)
- Test authentication middleware rejects unauthorized requests
- Test registration with existing email returns error
- Test login with invalid credentials returns error

## User Profile Tests
- Test getting user profile
- Test updating user display name
- Test that users cannot access other users' profiles

## Todo Creation Tests
- Test creating todo with valid title and optional fields
- Test creating todo with required title only
- Test creating todo with all optional fields
- Test creating todo without title returns validation error
- Verify newly created todos are incomplete by default
- Verify todo creation is associated with correct user

## Todo List Retrieval Tests
- Test paginated todo list retrieval
- Test single todo retrieval by ID
- Test single todo retrieval with full description
- Test that users only see their own todos
- Test unauthorized access to other users' todos is rejected

## Completion Status Tests
- Test marking todo as complete
- Test marking todo as incomplete
- Test toggle between complete and incomplete states
- Test completion status is reflected in todo list

## Todo Editing Tests
- Test editing todo title
- Test editing todo description
- Test editing todo start date
- Test editing todo due date
- Test editing multiple fields at once
- Test that edits create history entries
- Test editing non-existent todo returns error
- Test editing another user's todo is rejected

## Edit History Tests
- Test that each edit creates a history entry
- Test history entries contain correct timestamp
- Test history entries contain field change information
- Test history is sorted from most recent to oldest
- Test viewing another user's todo history is rejected
- Test that edit history is deleted when todo is permanently deleted

## Delete and Trash Tests
- Test soft delete of todo
- Test soft deleted todos don't appear in normal list
- Test soft deleted todos appear in trash list
- Test trash list is paginated
- Test restoring todo from trash returns it to normal list
- Test restored todo retains its properties
- Test permanent delete from trash
- Test permanent delete removes todo and its edit history
- Test permanent delete of non-existent todo returns error
- Test deleting another user's todo is rejected

## Filtering Tests
- Test filtering todo list by all todos
- Test filtering todo list by only complete todos
- Test filtering todo list by only incomplete todos
- Test filtering trash list
- Test invalid filter value returns error

## Sorting Tests
- Test sorting by creation date (newest first)
- Test sorting by creation date (oldest first)
- Test sorting by start date (earliest first)
- Test sorting by start date (latest first)
- Test sorting by due date (earliest first)
- Test sorting by due date (latest first)
- Test todos without start date appear at end when sorting by start date
- Test todos without due date appear at end when sorting by due date
- Test sorting with filtering combination
- Test sorting with pagination combination

## Privacy & Security Tests
- Test that all authenticated endpoints require valid token
- Test token expiration handling
- Test user cannot access any data owned by other users
- Test cascade deletion when user account is deleted

scenario.draft:
Test the primary success path of guest account registration. The test should:

1. Send a registration request with valid email format (RFC 5322), strong password (8+ characters), display name (2-20 characters), and session context (href and referrer URLs).

2. Verify the system creates a new guest account in the todo_app_guests table with the provided credentials.

3. Verify the password is properly hashed using bcrypt before storage.

4. Verify the system generates and returns JWT tokens (access token with 15-minute expiration, refresh token with 7-day expiration).

5. Verify the system creates a session record in todo_app_guest_sessions table with device tracking information.

6. Verify the returned guest account ID matches the ID in the authorization token.

7. Verify the newly created account is in active state and ready for immediate use.

8. Verify the email is stored with case-insensitive uniqueness constraint applied.

The test validates that a valid registration request transitions a guest from unauthenticated to authenticated status with full member access to todo functionality.

dependencies.purpose:
Essential authentication prerequisite:
This join operation (post /todoApp/auth/guest/join) must be executed before any operations requiring 'guest' actor authorization.
It establishes the necessary user account and authentication context for the 'guest' actor, enabling subsequent API calls that depend on this specific authorization level.
Without this join operation, the main scenario endpoint and its dependencies will fail due to insufficient authentication credentials.

functions.name: test_api_guest_registration_success

scenario.draft:
Test that successful guest registration creates a valid authenticated session for subsequent protected API operations.

1. Register a new guest account with valid credentials (email and password) and session context.

2. Verify the registration succeeds and returns guest account identification information including guestId.

3. Verify the response includes access token, refresh token, and their expiration timestamps.

4. Use the access token to make an authenticated request to a protected endpoint (e.g., retrieve member profile).

5. Verify the authenticated request succeeds with the received access token.

6. Verify the refresh token can be used to obtain new access tokens without re-login.

7. Verify the guest can continue authenticated operations across multiple API calls without re-entering credentials.

This test validates the complete registration-to-authentication workflow, ensuring the guest account is properly established and can be used for subsequent protected API operations.

Call the refresh endpoint with a valid refresh token that has not yet exceeded the refreshable_until deadline (7 days from creation). Verify the system returns new access and refresh tokens in the IAuthorized response with updated expired_at and refreshable_until timestamps. Confirm the new access token is immediately usable for protected endpoints. Validate that the session record in todo_app_guest_sessions table is updated with the new token values. scenario.draft:
Test successful member login with valid credentials. This scenario verifies the primary authentication workflow where an authenticated member can access their private todo workspace.

Test Steps:
1. Call /todoApp/auth/member/join to create a new member account with a valid email address and password
2. Capture the created member's credentials (email and password)
3. Call /todoApp/auth/member/login with the registered email and password
4. Verify the response contains valid JWT tokens (access and refresh)
5. Verify the response includes member information (id, email, display_name)
6. Verify access token expiration is set to 15 minutes
7. Verify refresh token expiration is set to 7 days
8. Verify a new session record was created in the database with the request's IP address, href, and referrer
9. Verify the member can now access member-only endpoints using the access token

Expected Results:
- Login succeeds with HTTP 200 status

scenario.draft:
Test that cross-user access to todo updates is properly rejected. This scenario validates that members cannot modify todos owned by other users, enforcing data isolation and privacy.

Prerequisites:

2. Attempt to update member A's todo by sending PUT request to /todoApp/member/todos/{todoId} with updated title and description
3. Verify the request is rejected with appropriate error response:
   - HTTP status code 403 Forbidden (access denied due to ownership violation)
   - Error message indicates lack of permission or ownership
4. Verify the todo remains unchanged:
   - GET request to /todoApp/member/todos/{todoId} using member A's token returns original values
   - GET request using member B's token should also reject (403 Forbidden)
5. Verify that no EditHistory entry was created for this rejected update attempt
6. Verify that member B's own todos list does not include the target todo (enforced isolation)

Success criteria:
- PUT request returns 403 Forbidden
- Todo ownership is enforced (no modification allowed)
- No edit history created for unauthorized attempt
- Data isolation maintained between members
- Each member can only see and modify their own todos

7. Test that the todo can be restored via POST /todoApp/member/todos/{todoId}/restore, then subsequently updated

- Soft delete lifecycle properly enforced

# Multi-User Todo Application - Implementation Requirements

## Implementation Scope

Implement the complete NestJS service layer for all API endpoints defined in the interface specifications.

## User Authentication & Account Services

### Register Service
- Validate email format and password strength
- Hash password using bcrypt or similar
- Create user record with unique email constraint
- Return user data with authentication token

### Login Service
- Validate email and password
- Verify password hash
- Generate JWT token
- Return user data and token

### Logout Service
- Invalidate JWT token (blacklist if implemented)
- Return success response

### Password Change Service
- Verify current password
- Validate new password strength
- Update password hash
- Return success confirmation

### Account Deletion Service
- Delete all user's todos (including trash)
- Delete user's edit history
- Delete user profile
- Delete user account
- Return confirmation

## User Profile Services

### Get Profile Service
- Return current user's profile (display name, email, created_at)
- Include all user fields

### Update Profile Service
- Update user's display name
- Validate input
- Return updated profile

## Todo Management Services

### Create Todo Service
- Validate required fields (title)
- Accept optional fields (description, start date, due date)
- Set completion status to false (incomplete) by default
- Associate todo with authenticated user
- Return created todo

### List Todos Service
- Implement pagination (limit, offset/page)
- Apply filtering by completion status (all, complete, incomplete)
- Apply sorting by:
  - Creation date (asc/desc)
  - Start date (asc/desc) - todos without start date at end
  - Due date (asc/desc) - todos without due date at end
- Filter to current user's todos only
- Return paginated response with metadata

### Get Single Todo Service
- Validate todo ID
- Verify ownership (current user owns this todo)
- Return todo with full details including description

### Update Todo Service
- Validate todo ID exists and belongs to current user
- Accept optional updates to title, description, start date, due date
- Create EditHistory entry for each field that changed
- Return updated todo

### Mark Complete Service
- Validate todo ID exists and belongs to current user
- Set completion status to true
- Return updated todo

### Mark Incomplete Service
- Validate todo ID exists and belongs to current user
- Set completion status to false
- Return updated todo

### Delete Todo Service (Soft Delete)
- Validate todo ID exists and belongs to current user
- Set deletedAt timestamp (soft delete)
- Todo no longer appears in normal list
- Return success confirmation

### Edit History Service
- Retrieve all history entries for a specific todo
- Verify todo belongs to current user
- Sort by timestamp descending (most recent first)
- Return list of history entries

## Trash Services

### List Trash Service
- Retrieve todos where deletedAt is set
- Filter to current user's deleted todos
- Implement pagination
- Return paginated trash list with metadata

### Restore Todo Service
- Validate todo ID exists and belongs to current user
- Verify todo is in trash (deletedAt is set)
- Set deletedAt to null (remove soft delete)
- Return restored todo

### Permanently Delete Service
- Validate todo ID exists and belongs to current user
- Verify todo is in trash
- Delete all associated EditHistory entries (cascade)
- Delete todo from database (hard delete)
- Return success confirmation

## Authorization Middleware

All endpoints must:
- Require valid JWT token
- Extract user ID from token
- Apply ownership checks on all user-specific operations
- Return 401 for unauthorized requests
- Return 403 when user tries to access another user's data

## Error Handling

- Validate all inputs
- Return 400 for validation errors
- Return 404 for not found resources
- Return 401 for unauthorized requests
- Return 403 for forbidden operations (accessing another user's data)
- Return 500 for unexpected errors

## Code Quality Standards

- TypeScript strict type checking
- Comprehensive error handling
- Input validation using class-validator decorators
- Transaction handling for cascade operations
- Consistent naming conventions
- JSDoc comments for all public methods
- Dependency injection pattern
- No hardcoded values
